builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LoGRA: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Sketches
summary: LoGRA replaces dense optimizer gradients in RL post-training with low-rank gradient sketches used for both model updates and policy synchronization, paired with predicted-KL step control that scales updates to limit policy drift. The cost is added implementation complexity (sketching, KL prediction, integration via the Molt library) and the demonstrated configuration is an eight-GPU node, well beyond a single 24 GB card. Compression can fail if low-rank sketches discard learning signal on tasks with ill-conditioned gradient structure, and the KL-step controller can misestimate policy change, destabilizing training.
rationale: The memory savings are real and relevant, but the validated setup requires an eight-GPU node and RL post-training infrastructure the reader does not have, so it is worth tracking rather than adopting now.
technique: Low-rank gradient sketches for RL post-training

claims.statement: LoGRA replaces dense optimizer gradients in RL post-training with low-rank gradient sketches used for both model updates and policy synchronization, paired with predicted-KL step control that scales updates to limit policy drift. The cost is added implementation complexity (sketching, KL prediction, integration via the Molt library) and the demonstrated configuration is an eight-GPU node, well beyond a single 24 GB card. Compression can fail if low-rank sketches discard learning signal on tasks with ill-conditioned gradient structure, and the KL-step controller can misestimate policy change, destabilizing training.

Reduces average RL training memory by up to 45.7% without sacrificing performance, enabling stable 27B-parameter RL training for over 1,100 steps on a single eight-GPU node where dense Adam runs out of memory.
